title: Daily market context

Colour limits are printed on the colour bar; associations are small and not causal.

title: U.S. → INDIA | Decision-aligned return association

caption: Numbered markers identify record improvements within the available retrospective Epoch mapping, not every frontier release. The plot ends in June 2025 to match that evidence. title: What happened around the mapped frontier advances?

U.S. close-to-close and Indian open-to-close returns cover different horizons, so magnitudes are not a like-for-like causal comparison. Reaction sessions follow the conservative publication-time mapping. Entries are observed returns, not market-adjusted abnormal returns. This is the limited Epoch-mapped subset shown in the timeline, not the complete 2026 event calendar.
change: Adds provider marks and model names, preserves readable country separation, and discloses unequal return horizons.
title: Observed U.S. and Indian reactions

caption: Recorded 2025 returns are 5.16% gross and -4.038% net. Both paths use identical holdings and execution dates. The shaded terminal wealth gap includes foregone compounding and is not simply the sum of cash fees. Costs are the implementation's assumed 7.5 bps per side, charged on turnover. 2026 is January–September; the joined path crosses from quarterly refits to a fixed-fit extension.
change: New cost-isolation figure with exact ledger accounting; replaces illustrative unverified gross numbers.
title: The same trades, before and after costs

caption: One continuous compounded path across 2025 and the January–September 2026 extension. The dashed line identifies the change in refit protocol, not a capital reset. Model returns include recorded trading costs. ETF and fixed-share current-cohort buy-and-hold comparisons include overnight exposure and do not receive the intraday strategy cost model; the cohort has current-membership selection bias.

title: Combined evaluation and passive alternatives

caption: Daily gross long and short exposures are shown with opposite signs. The lower panel counts actual sessions classified as long-only, short-only, mixed or flat. A flat month or session is retained rather than omitted. The policy allows simultaneous long and short positions even if the observed ledger contains none.

title: What was actually traded

caption: Counterfactual cost deductions on the exact same recorded decisions; forecast hurdles and holdings are never recalculated. At the modeled 15 bps round-trip cost, 2025 returns -4.04% net; its fixed-holdings break-even cost is approximately 8.25 bps. The January–September 2026 extension breaks even near 36.21 bps. These are unchanged-holdings descriptive stress tests, not optimized fee choices.
change: New fixed-holdings sensitivity avoids confusing cost-induced policy changes with pure cost drag.
title: How much trading friction can the strategy withstand?

caption: Screening and confirmation cells show the best observed net Sharpe within each family and the number of searched configurations. The 2025 and 2026 columns are frozen-period evaluations rather than new family searches; 2026 uses one pre-2026 fit with no reselection. Grey means not evaluated. Families with no finite trading Sharpe in every displayed stage are omitted rather than represented as zero.

title: Model families and selection stages

caption: Numerically sorted prediction deciles are plotted against mean realized Nifty IT constituent open-to-close returns. Points are intentionally unconnected: no fitted calibration curve is implied. Error bars are one date-clustered standard error and all endpoints are included in the shared axis limits; they preserve common shocks across stocks but are not simultaneous confidence bands. Historical bins contain 240–253 stock-day observations and extension bins 180–190. Dashed vertical lines mark the ±15 bps trading hurdle and the dotted diagonal marks perfect calibration. Neither panel establishes a stable calibration map.
change: Includes every uncertainty endpoint in the axis calculation, removes curve-like connecting lines and reports compact bin-count ranges.
title: Forecast magnitude is weakly calibrated

caption: The exact selected depth-6 Extra Trees specification is refitted after excluding all 60 fallback-flagged F7 columns; zero flagged columns remain. Bars compare cumulative net returns. The paired forest plot uses identical sessions and a 2,000-draw circular 10-session date-block bootstrap. Both mean-difference intervals cross zero, so the improved strict-vintage point estimates are robustness evidence rather than proof of superiority.
change: Replaces the pending architecture caveat with a completed, exact-specification empirical sensitivity.
title: Strict-vintage sensitivity

caption: Each column compares the same dates and stocks at ridge penalty 0.1. Positive R² improves on the rolling asset-mean forecast; negative R² worsens it. Screening covers 2021–2022, confirmation 2023–2024 and historical replication 2025. Raw constituent expansion usually increases error. This is evidence about this fixed linear specification, not all possible models or optimally tuned penalties.
change: Adds temporal context and matched quarterly comparisons in place of a single-period aggregate.
title: Feature additions across five annual evaluations

caption: Conditional U.S.-services coefficients control for lagged Indian-cohort and Nifty50 returns. Blue denotes Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 within the declared analysis batch; intervals are pointwise. A +1% U.S. return corresponds to approximately +0.098 percentage points in the full-sample Indian intraday outcome. Annual differences are not themselves significant: the direct period-interaction test was inconclusive. This is exploratory association, not causality.
change: Adds effect uncertainty and adjusted evidence; distinguishes association from profitable prediction.
title: Association can exist without a profitable strategy

caption: Marked Indian sessions by year are 2021: 0, 2022: 0, 2023: 5, 2024: 12, 2025: 7, 2026: 22. The 2026 calendar now uses dated official-provider announcements through 30 September under a fixed general-purpose frontier-release rule. Same-session releases can map to one Indian session, so session counts need not equal release counts. Small annual event samples still limit power and do not establish causal effects.
change: Uses the audited 2026 calendar and no longer labels observed zero coverage as an economic result.
title: Why later-period event conclusions remain unresolved

caption: Calendar-period cumulative net returns for the selected Extra Trees specification are 2021 +8.31%, 2022 +0.11%, 2023 +6.26%, 2024 +9.93%, 2025 -4.04%, 2026 +15.01%; 2026 ends on 30 September and is not a full-year return. The same configuration identifier is evaluated throughout, but each protocol stage uses its declared rolling or fixed-fit estimator. The 2021–2024 observations influenced model search and confirmation and are not holdout evidence; 2025 is a historical replication and 2026 is a retrospectively inspected fixed-specification extension. The wide 2025 and 2026 bootstrap Sharpe intervals prevent a stable-alpha claim.
change: Expands the stability view to the complete 2021–September 2026 protocol and clearly separates selection-exposed years from later evaluation.
title: One specification across search, confirmation, replication, and extension

caption: Dots show individual 2025–September 2026 monthly model returns; orange strokes are group means. Regimes use realized Nifty IT ETF monthly returns: rising ≥3%, falling ≤−3%, otherwise sideways. A reversal changes the latest non-sideways direction. These labels are known after the month ends and are descriptive, not pre-trade signals. Small reversal groups cannot establish reliable regime-specific skill.
change: Replaces bare three-bar regime summaries with individual observations, group sizes and explicit ex-post classification.
title: Sideways markets and reversals: observed monthly outcomes

caption: Grouped permutation importance rebuilt directly from the pinned 2025 and 2026 selected-model CSVs. Each repetition permutes a feature group by whole dates while preserving asset identities. Points are mean OOS MSE increases; bars are one standard deviation across repetitions and, in 2025, refits. They are descriptive variability, not confidence intervals. Positive values indicate predictive reliance; negative values can arise from finite-sample noise. The diagnostic is not a causal or isolated feature contribution.
change: Rebuilt from raw pinned CSVs; removes the legacy-PNG dependency and corrects the permutation-method description.
title: Exploratory model reliance
